The whole-base lift preserves the appropriate budget and weakly lowers depth, so the finite set over which cardinality is minimized is nonempty. Closed traces identify each proper closed minor of B with a closed subset of the original base after composition, and the next lift is affinely equivalent to the lift of that subset.

If the inherited lattice is restricted to the direction space of a minor, parity equivalence of retained sites is unchanged because the half-difference lies in that direction space. Integer graph projection and the congruence result then preserve parity counts under lifting even when affine rank increases. Helly equality and monotonicity follow from the closed-trace result.

A disconnected selected base has a component with M_i/q_i≥M/q by exact additivity. The restriction and lift comparison then gives D_(lift of component)<τ/q_i. Its unrestricted infimum is at most that tested depth, contradicting the cardinality choice. This holds for either budget and every smallest bad choice, with no assumed attainment at this step.

Every proper nonempty closed T has unrestricted lifted infimum at least τ/q(T) by the same cardinality choice. Testing the actual retained fibers and using the restriction and lift inequalities gives D_B≥M_T τ/q(T) at mass one. D_B≤δ<τ/q(B) gives the full displayed quota including its strict last inequality.

If the infimum of fiber masses across the sublevel were zero, a sequence of least masses tending to zero would have a convergent mass vector. Its positive support is nonempty by mass one, proper by finiteness and the vanishing least mass, and closed by scaled-source inclusion. Its retained mass tends to one, contradicting its fixed quota bounded by δ q(T)/τ≤δ q(B)/τ<1.

The floor and connectedness give uniformly bounded diameters after determinant-one anchor maps. Canonicality makes the position correction an invertible affine shear on the same base product. Both operations preserve total mass, compatibility, and normalized depth. Blaschke compactness and finiteness yield simultaneous limits, and compatibility passes by choosing convergent source points for each fixed representation. Volume and depth continuity preserve the mass-one positive sublevel.

Choose β<δ<τ/q(B), dilate a minimizing sequence to unit total mass, and take the compact tail. This attains the unrestricted infimum on B. A largest fiber has mass at least 1/|B|, and its centroid supplies at least γ_d/|B| to each containing ambient halfspace, including a pure-base cut that contains its whole fiber.

For an actual mixed-integer convex body the positive sites are finite and nonempty at positive total mass, and complete by scaled-source inclusion. Removing zero-volume fibers preserves all cap masses and only reduces the feasible marks, so the retained maximum is at most the original one. Its inherited parity count is at most 2^n, making the given strict body bound sufficient. Compatibility and inherited-lattice completeness realize the selected family as the exact mixed-integer trace of its placed hull. A rank-zero selected base causes no exception.

For rank r≥1, the r+1 facets of a simplex spanned by sites have empty total intersection and after deleting one have its opposite vertex as witness. This gives h(B)≥r+1. For rank zero a singleton has h(B)=1. Verified archived digests and locators for c280bb0dcfd30f3d §1 and §§4–8 and for 2086e4eaa4bce465 §6. The normalized statement generalizes their fixed threshold to any τ>0 and strengthens a minimizing-sequence floor to a uniform sublevel floor by the same valid quota argument.
